subject: Re: Model fit & prompt collection \u001a Acme next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Lawrence <tom.lawrence@acme.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit discovery  Acme / next steps

Tom / Sarah,

Thanks again for the call today  really helpful to understand Acme's search summarization workflow and the high-sensitivity content you mentioned (support transcripts, billing info). Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- What we heard: you need a summarization endpoint that preserves key policy facts, redacts PII by default, and runs at p50 latency <120ms for 512-token inputs. You want to avoid hallucinations on legal/financial snippets.
- Initial model recommendations: Redwood-1-medium-quant (fast/cheap starting point) and Redwood-1-large (baseline quality) for higher-fidelity cases. We'll run both in our eval harness.
- Benchmarks we'll run: Rouge/Lexical overlap, factuality checks (QA-based), and a custom regen test for policy-sensitive tokens.

Request for you: can you share a sample of ~50 representative prompts (real user inputs) including edge cases (screenshots redacted if necessary) so we can prioritize the prompt set? I've attached a small template CSV to make this easy. Please mark any rows that *must* be redacted or replaced with placeholders.

Next steps / timeline:
1) You share sample prompts + redaction notes (by EOD Thu 7/30)  acme_sample_prompts.txt or the attached CSV.
2) We run a 2-model eval (Redwood-1-medium-quant, Redwood-1-large) against your prompts and return a brief report with quality/regression flags (target: 48 hours).
3) If you want, we can run an internal prompt-redaction pass and provide a suggested redaction mapping you can push to the app.

Attachments: prompt_set_template.csv (simple CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, edge_case_tags, redaction_flag)

Anything I missed? Happy to hop on a quick 15m call to review sample prompts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference  production-first inference runtime

Thanks Marissa  good summary. We'll pull a representative set and flag PII as you suggested. Couple of quick clarifications: 

- For the eval, what specific metrics should we expect in the report? Sarah and I want a clear go/no-go threshold.
- On retention: our security team will ask what logs/redacted payloads Redwood retains during eval runs and how long. Can you confirm retention policy or who on your side can provide SOC/Security answers?

I'll aim to get the sample prompts into the CSV by EOD Thu. If we think there are more than 50, we'll send a prioritized 50 and a second bucket.

Tom
Director of Product  Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Lawrence <tom.lawrence@acme.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Model fit discovery  Acme / next steps (prompt set + security questions)

Dylan / Dev  forwarding Tom's note + the attached template. Can you help with two things: 

1) Dev: once Tom drops the CSV, can you spin up a short eval job (2-model) against the 50 prompts and share the preliminary quality dashboard + a short note on token cost estimate? Target: 48 hours after we receive the CSV. Please use the standard eval_config.yaml (attached) and include the following metrics: ROUGE-L, QA-factuality pass rate, and a hallucination detection score.

2) Dylan: can you provide clear redaction guidance we can send back to Acme? Specifically: a) suggested placeholder rules for account numbers / SSNs / email addresses, b) whether we should use token replacement vs placeholder text, and c) any prompt-side sanitization you recommend that doesn't harm summarization quality. If there's a short internal doc, paste the link.

Tom / Sarah: we'll also answer your retention question  tagging Security to make sure we include the SOC2/retention blurb in the eval report.

Attachments forwarded: prompt_set_template.csv, eval_config.yaml

Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Lawrence <tom.lawrence@acme.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Model fit discovery  Acme / next steps (prelim eval findings)

Quick update after a first pass (I used a small sample Tom uploaded to the shared drive):

- Setup: ran Redwood-1-medium-quant and Redwood-1-large across 30 prompts (subset) using eval_config.yaml.
- Preliminary metrics (subset):
  - ROUGE-L: med-quant 0.48 | large 0.62
  - QA factuality pass: med-quant 72% | large 90% (QA based on 5 ground-truth checks we constructed)
  - Hallucination detector flagged ~6% of med-quant outputs, ~2% of large outputs
- Cost estimate: med-quant ~0.9 tokens/output-unit avg; large ~2.7 tokens/output-unit avg (rough internal cost model)  estimate for full 50-prompt run: med-quant ~$45 | large ~$130.

Risks / notes:
- Quality regressions are likely in med-quant for edge-case legal/financial snippets. If Acme needs consistent fidelity, we should recommend Redwood-1-large for the top ~15% of highest-sensitivity prompts and med-quant for everything else.
- Redaction guidance: preferring explicit token-replacement placeholders (e.g., [ACCOUNT_NUM]) rather than tokenization-based removal  preserves context for summarization. Dylan: can you confirm whether we have a short template we can share?

Next steps:
- If we have permission from Tom, I'll run the full 50-prompt eval overnight and upload the full dashboard (Drive link) + a short deck summarizing recommended routing (per-prompt model selection + redaction mapping).

Drive (prelim): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmark-doc-ACME-2026
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-1243

Dev Patel
Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
